newsitem.title: USA: Fuji battles U.S. WTO film case in cyberspace.
newsitem.headline: Fuji battles U.S. WTO film case in cyberspace.

text.p: Fuji Photo Film Co has moved to cyberspace with a public relations campaign against a complaint by Eastman Kodak Co that Japan has thwarted foreign competition in its photo film market.

Fuji has established a new Internet site devoted to the case brought to the World Trade Organization by the U.S. government on behalf of Kodak. Located at http://home.fujifilm.com/wto/index.html, the site includes Fuji's 565-page rebuttal to Kodak's original allegations and an analysis of Japan's submissions to the WTO on the case.
The site also includes links to pages entitled "Kodak Mistakes in Japan" and "Hidden Facts" as well as an archive of documents and press releases by Fuji about the case.

Many of the documents had already been available through Fuji's home page, but a spokesman for Fuji said the company decided to make a separate web page to serve as a clearinghouse for information as a WTO dispute settle panel gets close to making a decision on the case later this year.

"It's clearly a link to Fuji propaganda," said Kodak spokesman Charles Smith. He said Kodak documents and press releases on the case are available through its home page http://www.Kodak.com, but the company does not have a single site devoted to the dispute.
Both Fuji and Kodak have engaged in heavy public relations campaigns about the case since Kodak first voiced its complaint two years ago.
